name: BRAZIL

flag.title: Flag of Brazil
flag.note: Green, gold diamond, blue globe & stars

lead: Brazil is the giant of South America. It borders almost every other country there. The Amazon, the world's largest tropical rainforest, grows here. Brazil is loud, colourful, and full of life.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Brazil holds 60% of the Amazon rainforest. The Amazon River pours more fresh water into the sea than any other river.
Beyond the jungle lie vast grasslands called the Cerrado. The Pantanal is the world's largest wetland. Iguaçu Falls is wider than Niagara Falls.
animals: Jaguars, pink river dolphins, and giant anteaters live in the Amazon. So does the capybara, the world's largest rodent. It looks like a giant guinea pig.
Piranhas and giant arapaima fish swim in the rivers. The Pantanal has the densest jaguar population on Earth.
culture: Brazil gave the world samba, bossa nova, and football legends like Pelé. Carnival is the biggest street party on the planet. Two million people a day join Rio's drumming, dancing parades.
Churrasco piles grilled meats high. Feijoada, a black-bean and pork stew, is the national dish.
history: Portugal ruled Brazil from 1500 and gathered sugar, gold, and rubber. Millions of Africans were enslaved and brought here. That painful past still shapes Brazil's music, food, and culture.
Brazil declared independence in 1822. A Portuguese prince became its first emperor. In 1960, the modern capital Brasília opened on an empty plateau.
wows: Brazil is the only Portuguese-speaking country in the Americas.
You can drink from the Atlantic 160 km offshore, thanks to the Amazon's fresh water.
Brazil has won the FIFA World Cup five times, more than any other nation.
Iguaçu Falls is nearly 3 km wide and has 275 separate waterfalls.
São Paulo has more Japanese-descended residents than any city outside Japan.
The Pantanal floods to the size of France every wet season.
Brasília was built in 41 months and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.

myths.myth: The Amazon makes 20% of Earth's oxygen
myths.fact: Not true. Amazon life uses nearly all the oxygen its trees make. The forest mainly stores carbon dioxide, a gas that warms Earth.
Piranhas mostly eat fish, insects, and seeds. They rarely bite unless starving or trapped.
